sources.entry: Supabase | Postgres development platform with auth, storage, realtime and edge functions

summary.one_liner: Supabase is an open source Postgres development platform that aims to offer Firebase-style features (database, auth, APIs, storage, realtime, functions) built on open source tools.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a Postgres-based backend with auto-generated REST and GraphQL APIs, realtime subscriptions that stream database changes over websockets, database functions and Edge Functions, file storage, and an AI/vector embeddings toolkit, plus a dashboard. Authentication and authorization are provided via GoTrue, a JWT-based auth API. Storage is described as a RESTful API for managing files in S3, with Postgres handling permissions. The README lists supporting components: PostgREST for the REST API, pg_graphql for GraphQL, postgres-meta for managing Postgres, Realtime (an Elixir server), and Envoy as an edge proxy. Client libraries are listed for JavaScript/TypeScript, Flutter, Swift, Python, C#, Go, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, Rust and Godot, with some marked official and others community-maintained. The README states it is a hosted platform, and that it can also be self-hosted and developed locally.
use_cases: Build a backend with Postgres, auth and file storage without writing a server
Expose a Postgres database as a REST or GraphQL API
Add realtime database change subscriptions to an app
Run serverless Edge Functions alongside a database
Store and search vector embeddings for AI features
how_to_run: Sign up for the hosted platform at supabase.com (no installation required, per the README)
For self-hosting and local development, see the documentation at supabase.com/docs
stack: Flutter, Swift, Python, Kotlin, C#, Go, Java, Ruby, Rust, Godot client libraries
notable: Built as a combination of existing open source tools (PostgREST, GoTrue, pg_graphql) rather than a single codebase
Offers a Firebase-like developer experience, but the README says it is not a one-to-one mapping of Firebase
Modular client libraries, each a standalone implementation for one system (auth, realtime, storage, functions)
Includes AI and vector/embeddings tooling built on Postgres
caveats: The README does not describe self-hosting setup steps; it points to external documentation
Feature set is a combination of several services, so self-hosting involves multiple components (per the architecture section)
Some client libraries are community-maintained rather than official
